def-channel-sequence:
## Definition

For each integer $n\ge1$, let $(\mathcal X_n,\mathcal A_n)$ and $(\mathcal Y_n,\mathcal B_n)$ be measurable spaces and let $W_n$ be a probability kernel from the first space to the second ([[def-measure-kernel-and-probability-kernel]]). The sequence $(W_n)_{n\ge1}$ is a **channel sequence**, and $n$ is its blocklength. A length-$n$ transmission sends an input in $\mathcal X_n$ and produces an output with conditional law $W_n$. No consistency between different blocklengths is assumed.
def-discrete-memoryless-channel:
## Definition

A **finite discrete memoryless channel (DMC)** is the channel sequence [[def-channel-sequence]] with fixed finite nonempty input and output alphabets $\mathcal X,\mathcal Y$ (with every subset measurable) and one stochastic kernel $W(y\mid x)$ from $\mathcal X$ to $\mathcal Y$ ([[def-finite-stochastic-kernel]]). At every blocklength its input and output alphabets are $\mathcal X^n,\mathcal Y^n$, and its block kernel is
$$W^n(y^n\mid x^n):=\prod_{i=1}^n W(y_i\mid x_i).$$
Thus the same single-use transition law is applied independently at each coordinate, conditional on the input word. This page imposes no feedback or input-cost constraint.
lem-discrete-memoryless-channel-block-ke:
## Statement

For a finite DMC $W$ and every $n\ge1$, the block formula $W^n(y^n\mid x^n)=\prod_{i=1}^n W(y_i\mid x_i)$ is a stochastic kernel from $\mathcal X^n$ to $\mathcal Y^n$.
def-discrete-memoryless-channel-informat:
## Definition

For an input probability vector $P_X$ on $\mathcal X$ ([[def-finite-probability-vector]]), let $P_{XY}(x,y):=P_X(x)W(y\mid x)$ and $Q_{P_X}(y):=\sum_xP_X(x)W(y\mid x)$. Write $I(P_X;W):=I(X;Y)$ for this joint law, using [[def-it-finite-mutual-information]]. The **single-letter information capacity** is
$$C(W):=\sup_{P_X} I(P_X;W),$$
measured in nats per channel use. The finite-dimensional maximum is attained, as proved in [[lem-discrete-memoryless-channel-capacity-is-attained]].
def-fixed-length-channel-code:
## Definition

For a finite DMC $W$, a **length-$n$ code with $M$ messages** is a pair of maps $e:[M]\to\mathcal X^n$ and $d:\mathcal Y^n\to[M]$, where $n,M\ge1$ and $[M]:=\{1,\ldots,M\}$. A message $m$ is encoded as $e(m)$, passed through the block kernel $W^n$ of [[def-discrete-memoryless-channel]], and decoded as $d(Y^n)$. The encoder and decoder are deterministic; there is no feedback, and no input-cost constraint is imposed.
def-discrete-memoryless-channel-informat:
## Definition

Given an input law $P_X$, let $Q_{P_X}=P_XW$ be its output law. The **information density** is
$$\imath_{P_X}(x;y):=\ln\frac{W(y\mid x)}{Q_{P_X}(y)}$$
when $P_X(x)W(y\mid x)>0$, and is $-\infty$ otherwise. For block sequences define $\imath_{P_X}(x^n;y^n):=\sum_{i=1}^n\imath_{P_X}(x_i;y_i)$, with any sum containing $-\infty$ equal to $-\infty$. On the support of the induced joint law, both numerator and denominator are positive, and the value is finite.
lem-discrete-memoryless-channel-capacity:
## Statement

For every finite DMC $W$, the supremum $C(W)$ is a maximum: there is an input probability vector $P_X^*$ such that $I(P_X^*;W)=C(W)$.
lem-discrete-memoryless-channel-n-letter:
## Statement

For every input probability vector on $\mathcal X^n$ and output $Y^n$ generated by a finite DMC $W^n$, one has $I(X^n;Y^n)\le nC(W)$.
def-fixed-length-channel-code-errors:
## Definition

For a length-$n$ code $(e,d)$, let
$$e_m:=W^n\{y^n:d(y^n)\ne m\mid e(m)\}.$$
Its **average error** is $\varepsilon_{\rm av}:=M^{-1}\sum_{m=1}^M e_m$, corresponding to a uniform message, and its **maximal error** is $\varepsilon_{\max}:=\max_{1\le m\le M}e_m$.
lem-discrete-memoryless-channel-iid-info:
## Statement

Fix a finite DMC $W$ and input law $P_X$. If $(X_i,Y_i)_{i\ge1}$ are IID with law $P_X(x)W(y\mid x)$, then $n^{-1}\imath_{P_X}(X^n;Y^n)\to I(P_X;W)$ in probability.
lem-discrete-memoryless-channel-capacity:
## Statement

Let $P_X^*$ attain $C(W)$ and let $Q^*:=P_X^*W$. If $W(y\mid x)>0$, then $Q^*(y)>0$, and for every $x\in\mathcal X$,
$$D(W(\cdot\mid x)\|Q^*)\le C(W).$$
def-discrete-memoryless-channel-operatio:
## Definition

A rate $R\ge0$ is **average-error achievable** for $W$ if there are length-$n$ codes for all sufficiently large $n$ with
$$\liminf_{n\to\infty}\frac{\ln M_n}{n}\ge R,\qquad \varepsilon_{\rm av}(n)\longrightarrow0.$$
It is **maximal-error achievable** if the same condition holds with $\varepsilon_{\max}(n)\to0$. Define $C_{\rm av}(W)$ and $C_{\max}(W)$ as the suprema of the respective achievable-rate sets. Rates use nats per channel use.
lem-discrete-memoryless-channel-average-:
## Statement

Every length-$n$ code with average error $\varepsilon_{\rm av}$ has a subcode with at least $M/2$ messages and maximal error at most $2\varepsilon_{\rm av}$.
thm-discrete-memoryless-channel-random-c:
## Statement

For every finite DMC $W$ and every $0\le R<C(W)$, there are fixed-length codes with $\liminf_{n\to\infty}n^{-1}\ln M_n\ge R$ and average error tending to zero.
lem-discrete-memoryless-channel-informat:
## Statement

Let $P_X^*$ attain $C(W)$ and $Q^*=P_X^*W$. There is a finite constant $V\ge0$ such that, for every $n\ge1$, every $x^n\in\mathcal X^n$, and every $\delta>0$, under output law $W^n(\cdot\mid x^n)$,
$$\Pr\left[\ln\frac{W^n(Y^n\mid x^n)}{(Q^*)^n(Y^n)}>n(C(W)+\delta)\right]\le\frac{V}{n\delta^2}.$$
The likelihood ratio is evaluated only on the support of $W^n(\cdot\mid x^n)$.
thm-discrete-memoryless-channel-average-:
## Statement

For any sequence of fixed-length codes over a finite DMC with average errors $\varepsilon_{\rm av}(n)\to0$, one has $\limsup_{n\to\infty}n^{-1}\ln M_n\le C(W)$.
thm-discrete-memoryless-channel-alphabet:
## Statement

Let $W$ be a finite DMC with finite nonempty input and output alphabets and no input-cost constraint. For any sequence of length-$n$ codes with $\liminf_{n\to\infty}n^{-1}\ln M_n>C(W)$, the average success probability tends to zero; hence both average and maximal error tend to one.
thm-discrete-memoryless-channel-capacity:
## Statement

For every finite DMC $W$ with no input-cost constraint,
$$C_{\rm av}(W)=C_{\max}(W)=C(W)=\max_{P_X}I(P_X;W),$$
with rates and mutual information measured in nats per channel use.
